svg.text: no mask, no reference, no hint
I am inspecting this small PCB module, which features a micro-USB port, a push button, and various
surface-mount components like resistors and capacitors. The blue solder mask appears mostly clean across
the central and top regions. I am checking the edges for quality control. Looking at the bottom edge,
specifically the light blue border area, I notice a distinct dark linear mark. This feature is situated
just below the gold-colored solder pads labeled 'BD1' and the pad near 'C5'. While the rest of the PCB
border is a uniform light blue, this dark, slanted line disrupts the surface continuity of the
substrate. It appears to be a physical scratch or crack in the board material rather than a stray silk-
screen mark. The rest of the board, including the solder joints and component placements, looks
standard. The anomaly at the bottom-center is a clear defect.
a normal trace carries no location or type tag, the format reward forbids them
counts are anomaly + normal, by true verdict
AnomalyThink-15K = union of all three splits, 14,472 traces (Ch. 6 ablation)
anomaly : normal in both training splits, by true verdict
stratified, about 100 + 100 per product in the SFT pool
no image appears in two splits, enforced by basename exclusion
so it is a generalisation check within Real-IAD, not a transfer test. MMAD (Ch. 4 to 6) is the transfer test.
Section 3 of the AnomalyThink construction: what one instance contains, and how the 14,472 traces are split.
